content.value_statement: Production ML work requires deployment, monitoring, and LLM integration across many tools. This skill provides templates and guidance for MLOps, model serving, RAG, and model monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Documents production ML architecture patterns for deployment, monitoring, security, and scalability.
Provides Python CLI scaffolds for model deployment, RAG system building, and ML monitoring workflows.
Outlines MLOps practices including MLflow, feature stores, drift detection, and automated retraining.
Guides RAG architecture choices such as chunking, vector databases, hybrid search, citations, and re-ranking.
Lists deployment and operations examples for Docker, Kubernetes, Helm, tests, formatting, and health checks.
limitations: The included Python scripts are scaffolds with placeholder execution logic.
It does not include trained models, datasets, cloud credentials, or production infrastructure.
Architecture guidance still requires validation against the user environment and compliance needs.
Command examples may need adaptation before use in a real deployment pipeline.

use_cases.title: Prepare a model deployment plan
use_cases.description: Design serving, scaling, monitoring, and rollback steps for a trained model.

use_cases.title: Convert a prototype into an MLOps workflow
use_cases.description: Map notebooks, models, and evaluation outputs into versioned production processes.

use_cases.title: Review RAG and LLM architecture
use_cases.description: Assess retrieval, caching, observability, access control, and deployment patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Start a deployment plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan deployment for a trained model. Ask for the model type, traffic target, latency target, cloud environment, and monitoring needs.

prompt_templates.title: Design model monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a monitoring plan for a production ML model. Include latency, errors, drift, data quality, alert thresholds, and rollback signals.

prompt_templates.title: Build a RAG architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RAG system for internal documents. Cover chunking, embeddings, vector storage, hybrid search, citations, evaluation, and access control.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an ML platform
prompt_templates.prompt: Review our ML platform architecture for production readiness. Focus on CI, model registry, feature stores, deployment safety, observability, cost, and security.

output_examples.input: Plan deployment for a classification model with low latency requirements.
output: Recommended serving architecture with containerized inference and autoscaling.
Latency and throughput targets mapped to monitoring metrics.
Release plan with canary rollout, rollback triggers, and health checks.
Security checklist for secrets, access control, and encrypted data paths.

output_examples.input: Design a RAG system for internal policy documents with citations.
output: Document ingestion plan with chunking, metadata, and access filters.
Retrieval design using vector search, keyword matching, and re-ranking.
Answer quality checks with citation coverage and confidence review.
Operations plan for indexing updates, monitoring, and cost tracking.

output_examples.input: Assess whether our model monitoring is production ready.
output: Gap analysis across drift, data quality, latency, errors, and business metrics.
Alert policy with severity levels and owner routing.
Retraining and rollback criteria linked to measurable thresholds.

best_practices: Define latency, reliability, and quality targets before choosing deployment tools.
Track model versions, data versions, and feature definitions through the full lifecycle.
Add monitoring for drift, data quality, service health, and business impact.
anti_patterns: Deploying a model without rollback, ownership, or incident response steps.
Treating offline validation metrics as enough evidence for production readiness.
Building RAG pipelines without citation checks, access controls, or retrieval evaluation.

faq.question: Does this skill train models?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on deployment, monitoring, MLOps, LLM integration, and architecture planning.

faq.question: Which frameworks are referenced?
faq.answer: The documentation references PyTorch, TensorFlow, Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LangChain, LlamaIndex, and DSPy.

faq.question: Can it deploy directly to my cloud account?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and scaffolds, but users must supply infrastructure, credentials, and environment details.

faq.question: What makes it useful for RAG systems?
faq.answer: It covers chunking, vector databases, hybrid search, citation support, re-ranking, and observability concerns.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated data?
faq.answer: It includes privacy and security considerations, but compliance decisions require domain review and legal approval.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
